html:
Ljudevit Gaj was a linguist and political leader, born in 1809 in Krapina in northern Croatia, who led the Croatian national revival known as the Illyrian movement.

In 1830 he proposed a reformed Latin alphabet for Croatian, borrowing letters with marks such as č and š from Czech, and it is the alphabet used today. He started a newspaper in 1835 and chose the Štokavian dialect, also spoken by Serbs, as the basis of a common written language for the South Slavs. The movement pushed back against Hungarian, which the Hungarian diet wanted to impose. In 1847 Croatian replaced Latin as the official language of the Croatian diet. Gaj's ideas fed both Croatian nationalism and the later idea of Yugoslavia.
